newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end little changed, volume low.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end little changed, volume low.

text.p: New York precious metals futures marginally lower Thursday, and volumes were very low, as the market winds down for the year.

"The Christmas and New Year holidays this year fall midweek for the next two weeks, effectively killing most trading from now until year end," North American Equity Services trader John Geraghty said.
"Some brokers are planning to leave town next week to visit clients instead," he said.
"The daily ranges are getting narrower and it's tough for the locals to make money right now," he said.
COMEX February gold ended down 20 cents at $371.10 an ounce, after trading in a $371.70-370.70 range. Estimated total volume was xx,xxx lots.
Spot gold in the bullion market ended quoted $369.00/50, down from the London Thursday afternoon fix at $369.00, but little changed from the New York close Wednesday at $369.10/369.60.
COMEX March silver closed down 0.8 cent at $4.885 an ounce, after seeing a 15 day intraday high Wednesday.
"As long as investment demand is sidelined, prices are not expected to post a strong upward move," CPM Group analyst Edward Kempf said.
NYMEX January platinum ended down $1.10 an ounce at $373.80, after seeing an eight day high intraday at $375.40.
The April platinum/gold spread ended at $2.80 an ounce, just off Wednesday's close at $3.20, but well off the week's lows at 10 cents.
NYMEX March palladium closed off 40 cents at $121.00.
In the past two weeks, the precious metals complex has been consolidating and recovering from the year's lows seen in late November.
Momentum oscillators, such as standard nine-day RSI (relative strength indicators and five-day stochastics, have been recovering from oversold levels.
But the year-long downtrend, which took gold prices to three year lows at $366 an ounce, have not been broken yet, analysts said.
